articles.title: "Women reporters will have a harder time": How one NFL scandal weaponized suspicion against women journalists who had nothing to do with it
articles.summary: NFL News: Mike Vrabel is back to coaching football. The New England Patriots are preparing for 2026. And for most people inside the league, the offseason drama .
articles.body: Mike Vrabel is back to coaching football. The New England Patriots are preparing for 2026. And for most people inside the league, the offseason drama surrounding Vrabel and former Athletic reporter Dianna Russini has faded into the background. But for a number of women who cover the NFL for a living, the fallout from that scandal has not gone anywhere. It has quietly reshaped how they do their jobs, who they feel comfortable talking to, and how much extra caution they now need to exercise just to do basic reporting work.Why are NFL women reporters saying source-building has become harder after the Vrabel-Russini scandal?The mechanics of sports journalism are built on access. Reporters need sources. Sources mean informal conversations, coffee meetings, sideline chats, late-night texts after a draft pick. None of that is unusual. It is the job.What has changed, according to multiple women reporters who spoke to ESPN, is that those ordinary interactions now carry a different weight. One assistant coach told a female reporter he would rather not meet her for coffee because he did not want people drawing conclusions about it after everything that happened with Vrabel and Russini. That is not a small thing. That is a gatekeeper closing a door that was already narrow to begin with.Another reporter said NFL personnel reached out to her this spring with a direct warning: "Women reporters will have a harder time at the scouting combine." The combine is one of the most important networking events of the football calendar. Losing ground there is a real professional cost.Four reporters told ESPN they feel they now have to be more deliberate about routine interactions. One said she has started telling her editor when she meets with team personnel, simply because she worries someone might photograph the meeting and it might be misread. These are the calculations that male reporters are not making.What makes it more painful is who was at the center of it. Vrabel had made a visible effort to treat women in the press corps with more respect than many of his peers. He gave the first question at news conferences to veteran female reporters, a habit he brought with him from Tennessee."It really [expletive] sucks that this came from someone who a lot of us thought approached things differently than his peers," one reporter who has covered Vrabel told ESPN. "It's just unfortunate because it felt like he understood there are challenges that women in the business face and was doing one small bit to try and push back on it."That context makes the irony hard to ignore. The one coach many of these reporters considered an ally is now the reason some of them feel more exposed than before.What happened to Dianna Russini and Mike Vrabel, and why did only one of them lose their career?Photos of Vrabel and Russini together at a resort in Sedona, Arizona, surfaced in April. Both said the images were taken out of context. Russini described a group outing. Vrabel called the suggestion of anything improper laughable. Within two weeks, Russini had resigned from The Athletic. Vrabel briefly left the Patriots during the NFL Draft to seek counseling and then came back.The Athletic launched an internal investigation that ran five months. It concluded that Russini's undisclosed relationship with Vrabel violated newsroom standards, though it found little evidence that her coverage was biased. She was still gone. He was still coaching.Vrabel went on to lead New England to the Super Bowl in his first season and enters 2026 with the Patriots circled as contenders again. For him, the story is essentially over.For the women who cover his team and the rest of the league, it is still unfolding in quieter, less visible ways. Every coffee meeting that does not happen, every source who pulls back, every extra email to an editor before a normal conversation with a coach, those are the real costs. They are not dramatic. They do not make headlines. But they compound.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Examining the last 5 Falcons quarterbacks to start Week 1
articles.summary: Who were the last 5 Falcons quarterbacks to start Week 1?
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons will enter the 2026 NFL season with a new starting quarterback for the sixth year in a row. Tua Tagovailoa will start in the team's Week 1 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, which feels like a decision made by default since Michael Penix Jr . has been ruled out.

Switching quarterbacks every year isn't a great strategy for winning games in the NFL, and the fact that the Falcons have won at least seven games in five straight seasons is actually kind of impressive (in a pathetic kind of way).

Starting in 2021, when Falcons president of football Matt Ryan was still the starting QB, here's a look at the last five quarterbacks to start for Atlanta in Week 1.

Passing: 3,968 yards, 20 TD, 12 INT, 90.4 rating

Ryan's final season in Atlanta was not one of his best, but he deserves credit for leading a bad team to seven wins. The Falcons' offensive line was not what it is today, and Ryan was sacked at least 40 times for the fourth year in a row. Atlanta traded Ryan to the Colts after the 2021 NFL season.

Passing: 2,219 yards, 15 TD, 9 INT, 88.1 rating

Mariota was signed as a bridge starter for the Falcons after the team traded Matt Ryan. The former No. 2 overall pick reunited with Arthur Smith but the results were underwhelming. Mariota's season wasn't as bad as people made it out to be, but his viral miscues made it clear he wasn't the long-term answer. Smith benched Mariota in favor of rookie Desmond Ridder, who stated the final four games that season.

Passing: 2,836 yards, 12 TD, 12 INT, 83.4 rating

Ridder was drafted by the Falcons in the third round of the 2022 NFL Draft (ahead of Malik Willis ), and was officially named the starter entering his second season. Ridder struggled with turnovers and reading NFL defenses. His athleticism wasn't the advantage many expected and he was benched for Taylor Heinicke multiple times throughout the season. After the season ended, the Falcons traded Ridder and brought in two new quarterbacks.

Passing: 3,508 yards, 18 TD, 16 INT, 88.6 rating

Cousins signed a four-year, $180 million contract with the Falcons a month before the team drafted Michael Penix Jr. After a hot start by Cousins, he had the worst four-game stretch of his career and lost his job to Penix with three games left in the season. The veteran QB passed for a career-high 16 interceptions in 14 games.

Passing: 1,982 yards, 9 TD, 3 INT, 88.5 rating

Penix tore his ACL against the Panthers in Week 11, but showed a good amount of upside in his nine games. While he struggled with some operational penalties and general inconsistency, Penix put the team in position to win multiple games. The Falcons' kicking woes likely cost Penix at least two wins, but the ACL injury was a devastating blow for the former No. 8 pick.

After a long, confusing quarterback competition, the Falcons named Tagovailoa as their Week 1 starter. The former Dolphins QB was released over the offseason after six seasons in Miami. While the media has treated Tagovailoa like a punching bag based on reports of a bad joint practice performance in Indianapolis, he completes a high percentage of his passes and doesn't turn the ball over a ton. However, Tua will have to play well to keep Penix off of his heels.

The Falcons and Steelers will kick things off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday in Pittsburgh.

articles.title: NFL execs predict Packers WR Matthew Golden as breakout player of 2026
articles.summary: Who might be the NFL's breakout player in 2026? Execs and scouts believe Packers WR Matthew Golden is a top candidate.
articles.body:
In a poll of NFL executives and scouts from ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Green Bay Packers receiver Matthew Golden was predicted as the NFL's "breakout player" of the 2026 season.

Golden is entering Year 2 with a starting job intact, more opportunities coming his way and a big chance to emerge as a game-changing player for the Packers.

From one AFC executive: "I'm not really sure why they didn't use him, but I loved him coming out. He can fly."

Other receiving votes for breakout player included Chargers running back Omarion Hampton, Bears tight end Colston Loveland, Buccaneers defensive lineman Calijah Kancey and Giants edge rusher Abdul Carter.

Last season, Golden battled through various minor injuries and a role complicated by a deep receiver room in Green Bay, finishing with 29 catches for 361 yards, and he didn't score his first pro touchdown until the NFC Wild Card Round in Chicago. Gone now are Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks, clearing the path for Golden to be a top contributor for Jordan Love and Matt LaFleur in 2026.

The big question: What would make Golden a true breakout player this season? Going over 1,000 receiving yards or catching 10 or more touchdowns would certainly qualify.

articles.title: How Bill Belichick’s silence on the UNC investigation is raising bigger questions about his control of the Tar Heels
articles.summary: NFL News: Bill Belichick is coaching college football without his defensive coordinator son, without his longtime general manager, and now with outside investig.
articles.body: Bill Belichick is coaching college football without his defensive coordinator son, without his longtime general manager, and now with outside investigators asking whether the people closest to him behaved appropriately inside his own program. When reporters asked him about it Monday, he gave them almost nothing. His son's absence is a medical matter he won't discuss. His conversations with Lombardi are private. His job, he said, is to coach football. That's where it stayed.What is the UNC football investigation about and who is involved?The investigation surfacing around UNC's football program covers more ground than a single allegation. Outside lawyers hired by the university have been asking witnesses whether Steve Belichick used drugs at university facilities or provided substances to at least one player. Those are questions being explored, not confirmed facts. Steve, who serves as defensive coordinator under his father, has been away from the program since early August on what UNC describes as medical leave. There is no confirmed date for his return.Michael Lombardi's exit added another layer. He had joined Belichick at Chapel Hill after years working alongside him in the NFL and in media. Placed on administrative leave in July, he resigned last week. The university said its investigation would continue regardless and that corrective action would follow depending on what the inquiry finds.Investigators reportedly asked witnesses about other matters too -- including an alleged sexual relationship between a recruiting staff member and a player, and possible relationships involving assistant coaches and recruiting personnel. Beyond individual allegations, people interviewed told reporters that investigators asked about the broader culture inside the program and whether questionable behavior had been reported upward to the head coach.That last part matters. It shifts the question from what certain staff members may have done to what Belichick knew or didn't know while leading the program. He addressed that indirectly. "I believe that everybody's responsible, including me, for doing things properly," he said. Whether that satisfies scrutiny depends on what the investigation ultimately surfaces.Is Bill Belichick's UNC program in serious trouble heading into year two?UNC opened this season with a 15-10 win over TCU in Ireland. It was a functional result, achieved without a defensive coordinator or general manager on the sideline. The Tar Heels now prepare for their home opener against East Tennessee State on September 12. Football has continued. The program has not stopped functioning.But the surrounding context is harder to brush aside. Belichick built his operation at Chapel Hill around a small group of trusted people. Two of the most significant are now gone or absent. The investigation has not concluded, and the university has reserved the right to take corrective action. When asked whether leadership had directed changes to how the program runs, Belichick was measured. "We want to run the program in the very best way," he said. "And if there's things we need to do to correct it, then we'll obviously do them."He is clearly trying to separate the football from the investigation. Whether that separation holds depends on how far the inquiry reaches.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body:
With the college season in full swing and the NFL season set to begin this week, one thing fans need to be made aware of are the various speciality concession items on the menu at stadiums around the country.

On the NFL side, the Indianapolis Colts' selections include football-shaped tater tots topped with a choice of Buffalo chicken, Philly cheesesteak or vegan street-style toppings.

They are also offering loaded footlong corn dogs, dirty sodas and a limited supply of carved prime rib sandwiches with the latter item featuring a live countdown inside Lucas Oil Stadium to let fans know how many remain.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Provided by Andy Reid, Latest on Chiefs QB's Status for NFL Week 1
articles.summary: After sitting out the entire preseason as part of his continued recovery from a torn ACL, Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback Patrick Mahomes received some good news.
articles.body:
After sitting out the entire preseason as part of his continued recovery from a torn ACL, Kansas City Chiefs star quarterback Patrick Mahomes received some good news.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters on Tuesday that Mahomes has a "pretty good" chance to start the team's season opener against the Denver Broncos on Monday Night Football .

Mahomes has been an active participant in practice throughout training camp, but it was no surprise that the Chiefs took a cautious approach with his recovery. Still, Reid sounded confident that the two-time NFL MVP will be under center when Kansas City opens the year against a Denver team that claimed the AFC West crown last season, ending its incredible run of nine straight division titles.

"As far as our roster goes, there's a very good chance that Patrick will go ahead and start unless something were to come up here in the next couple days," Reid told reporters . "Most likely he'll be the guy that's out there."

Mahomes tore his ACL last December, but he aggressively attacked his rehab with the goal of being ready for the start of the 2026 campaign. It was the first major injury of his impressive career, but the three-time Super Bowl champion refused to let it slow him down.

The Chiefs acquired quarterback Justin Fields from the New York Jets earlier this offseason to provide some extra insurance behind Mahomes, but they will surely need their longtime leader to be healthy if they want to return to title contention this year. It sounds like Mahomes is already on the right track, and Kansas City will be ready to start the year with a tough test against Denver.

articles.title: MarShawn Lloyd's Updated Fantasy Outlook as Packers OC Reveals Backfield Plan vs. Vikings
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers will be using a running back-by-committee "for a little bit" as the team moves forward without starter Josh Jacobs, who is unavailable for an undetermined amount of time after being placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers will be using a running back-by-committee "for a little bit" as the team moves forward without starter Josh Jacobs, who is unavailable for an undetermined amount of time after being placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List .

Packers offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich revealed that news to reporters on Tuesday.

Without Jacobs, the running back room consists of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson.

By all accounts, Lloyd figures to be the leader (he is No. 1 on the Ourlads and ESPN depth charts), although the "running back-by-committee" comment here could muddle the waters and potentially foreshadow a hindered fantasy outlook if Green Bay is going to give numerous snaps to Brooks and Johnson as well.

The latest FantasyPros point-per-reception (PPR) rankings, which serve as a consensus for 128 experts, currently list Lloyd at 106th overall (35th among running backs). His current average draft position (ADP) is 39th among running backs and 118th overall in 12-team PPR leagues, per Fantasy Football Calculator .

Lloyd played three years at South Carolina (2021 and 2022) and USC (2023) before the Packers selected him with a third-round choice in the 2024 draft.

His best collegiate season was 2023, when Lloyd amassed 1,052 yards and nine touchdowns on 129 touches. He rushed for 7.1 yards per carry and was highly efficient in the pass game (232 yards on just 13 receptions).

Unfortunately, Lloyd has dealt with a wave of ailments that has held him to just six carries. Per ESPN's Rob Demovsky , Lloyd suffered a hip injury in his rookie year training camp and a hamstring injury in his first preseason game. He didn't play Week 1 but had six carries for 15 yards in Week 2. Unfortunately, Lloyd suffered an ankle injury and went on injured reserve.

He was getting ready to return but then had an emergency appendectomy in November and then another hamstring injury following his recovery.

In 2025, Lloyd missed the Aug. 9 preseason game with a groin injury, but he then returned to preseason action on Aug. 16 and suffered a hamstring ailment after making a 33-yard catch against the Indianapolis Colts. He had two hamstring strains and a calf sprain in 2025 overall, per Demovsky .

Thankfully, Lloyd enters this year healthy, and he spent time in California this year with Dr. John Meyer of the Meyer Institute of Sport to get to the bottom of his issues, per packers.com senior writer Wes Hodkiewicz .

In sum, it was deemed Lloyd was "overcompensating in workouts to train his lower body" after suffering a torn ACL in 2020 while at South Carolina.

All told, there is certainly optimism about Lloyd. It's fair to wonder, though, how much the Packers would realistically push him. Simply put, he hasn't rushed the ball much over time, and no more than 129 times in a given year since high school.

Overall, Lloyd could very well be efficient, show explosiveness and stay healthy, and that would be a huge win for all.

From a fantasy standpoint, given the Packers OC's comments, coupled with the fact that it's hard to see Lloyd being given a workhorse role to avoid risking further injury, he may not be the best option.

At best, Lloyd seems like a flex, but realistically, he's solid depth as a bench option, simply because the opportunities may not be there.

articles.title: Who is Joy Taylor's mystery ex who cheated on her with another girl using her money?
articles.summary: NFL News: The former Fox Sports personality recently opened up about a past relationship in which she claims she financially supported her boyfriend only for hi.
articles.body: The former Fox Sports personality recently opened up about a past relationship in which she claims she financially supported her boyfriend only for him to allegedly use the money she gave him to go to a strip club and cheat on her. But Joy Taylor has left fans with one major question after revealing this explosive story about an ex-boyfriend: Who was he?Who is Joy Taylor’s ex-boyfriend? Sports host reveals he cheated with a stri**er using her moneyTaylor shared the story during an appearance on Get to the Point, hosted by Terrell Owens and Chris Spencer, where she was asked about one of the craziest relationship experiences she had ever gone through.According to Taylor, her former boyfriend was not working at the time and spent roughly a month sitting on the couch playing video games while she handled the bills. Eventually, she told him that he needed to get a job and gave him money to go out, get a drink, and clear his head. But instead of simply taking some time for himself, Taylor said he went to a strip club and allegedly cheated on her with a stri**er.The betrayal reportedly became even more shocking because Taylor said she was the person financially supporting him at the time.Taylor also explained how she allegedly found out.A bartender at the club recognized her boyfriend and reportedly alerted Taylor about what had happened. When confronted, Taylor said the man denied cheating and even suggested they go to the club together to find out what really happened.For Taylor, however, the situation was enough to end the relationship.The story has now sparked curiosity over the identity of the mystery man, particularly because Taylor did not name him while telling the story.Taylor has previously been involved in two high-profile relationships. She was married to former MLB player Richard Giannotti, with the pair marrying in 2016 before divorcing the following year. She was also engaged to former NBA player and coach Earl Watson before their relationship ended in 2019.However, there is no credible indication that either Giannotti or Watson was the man Taylor was describing in this particular story.That distinction is important because Taylor's comments have not publicly identified the ex, leaving the identity of the boyfriend she was discussing unclear.Rather than naming him, Taylor focused on the bizarre circumstances of the breakup, including the fact that she allegedly gave him money shortly before he used it during his night at the strip club.And there was one final detail that showed just how done she was with the relationship.Taylor joked that when she eventually left, she took almost everything because she had been paying for it anyway, leaving the ex with just one of their two brooms.For now, the identity of Taylor's mystery ex remains exactly that: a mystery.Unless Taylor decides to reveal his name herself, speculation about whether the story involved one of her publicly known former partners remains just that, speculation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rams? Seahawks? Bengals? The NFL's Best Teams Heading Into Week 1
articles.summary: Just one of last year's Super Bowl teams made Colin Cowherd's top 10; here's who he's most excited about heading into Week 1.
articles.body: Making it to Super Bowl LX isn't enough to reserve a spot in Colin Cowherd's top 10 – the first Herd Hierarchy before Week 1 of the 2026 regular season, shared on Tuesday's edition of "The Herd with Colin Cowherd," revealed as much. The New England Patriots aren't the only team missing, however: Cowherd made a point of saying that the Kansas City Chiefs and Baltimore Ravens were both close to making this inaugural list… but not close enough. There's plenty of season left for the teams missing from it now to play their way into the Hierarchy. But for now, here is Cowherd's actual top 10 before Week 1 kicks off – which includes Super Bowl LX's champions, at least. 10.Bengals Cowherd’s thoughts: "One of the most improved teams, and one of the teams that I thought made real moves, the Cincinnati Bengals. They’ve won the division the two times they’ve given Joe Burrow a top-20 defense. And by adding Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, Kyle Dugger, Cashius Howell and Boye Mafe, I think they’re going to have a top-20 defense. You also look in their division: old Aaron Rodgers twice, the Browns’ quarterback situation twice, I think when Burrow doesn’t have to only win by track meet, is a playoff quarterback." 9.Texans Cowherd’s thoughts: "Best defense in the league by a margin. Listen, they’ve won 10 of their last 11 games, I’m a fan of C.J. Stroud — though the last two years, too many mistakes — they return 10 of the 11 starters that made their defense and shut down the L.A. Rams. The Seahawks couldn’t even do that. I like the Texans a lot: Danielle Hunter, Will Anderson Jr., Derek Stingley Jr. are about as good as anybody in the league at their positions, and I love head coach DeMeco Ryans and their GM — they just can’t stay healthy at wide receiver." 8.Bears Cowherd’s thoughts: "Listen: 10-1 when they won the turnover battle. And here’s the good news: Caleb Williams doesn’t turn the ball over. He does not throw interceptions. He didn’t at USC, he doesn’t in the NFL, he didn’t in high school. And I think Colston Loveland, Luther Burden and Rome Odunze, as they now age, are going to become an elite, top of the league trio. Rome Odunze had a nice camp, he’s finally healthy. Do I worry about a lack of a consistent pass rush? Yes, that’s why I have the bears at No. 8. 7.Broncos Cowherd’s thoughts: "I think we’re overselling the fact that they trailed in a lot of games last year. Well, adding Jaylen Waddle, there’s a chance that will rejuvenate the passing game a little bit. They gave up the fewest sacks, and for two years in a row have led the NFL in sacks. They have an elite coach and returned 41 of their 43 offensive touchdowns. Yes, their schedule’s hard, yes, it’s a great coaching division, but I think Bo Nix is — and I think a lot of people are struggling to acknowledge — pretty good! He may not be great, but he’s pretty good." 6.Chargers Cowherd’s thoughts: "Worry about the interior O-line again, but I’m going to put the Chargers in — 11-6 last year, with the lowest-rated offensive line. They got an upgrade at offensive coordinator in Mike McDaniel, I think their weapons are good enough, they’ve added a rookie edge rusher with their first-round pick, Omario Hampton now healthy at running back — only team in the league top-five in third down and third down defense. Now they have the perfect coordinator for Justin Herbert." 5.Eagles Cowherd’s thoughts: "It gets real close now. Philadelphia, Week 1, big favorites against Washington. No. 2-ranked O-line, and you know what I say about O-lines. Hard not to make the playoffs when you have a top-5 or -6 O-line in the league. DeVonta Smith, is he a great No. 1 receiver with A.J. Brown gone? Well, they added Dontayvion Wicks and Hollywood Brown and Makai Lemon from USC (who had a spotty camp)... they’re good enough at wide receiver, great at running back, good at quarterback. Easy schedule, by NFC standards." 4.Lions Cowherd’s thoughts: "I think the Lions will battle for the Super Bowl. Easiest schedule in the league, they have a new offensive coordinator that’s viewed in-house as an upgrade, their skill positions — Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Sam Laporta and Jameson Williams are really, really electric playmakers. That matters in the long NFL season, you can’t have 13-play drives, week after week. You need some over the top home runs by Jahmyr Gibbs or Williams. Great teams get occasional easy touchdowns; not everything are perfect long drives. 3.Bills Cowherd’s thoughts: "I like Buffalo more than most, largest favorites to win their division. Josh Allen is 28-8 against his division — it’s got a Tom Brady feel. They traded for D.J. Moore — because he’s not flashy and not terribly demonstrative, people don’t understand how good he is. Durable, professional, open — I love D.J. Moore, a real serious No. 1 receiver. We gotta be honest about this: their rush defense was bad. But the last two years, they’ve spent more draft picks on defensive capital than any other team. I think some of those start to pay off." 2.Rams Cowherd’s thoughts: "The Rams are the most talented team in football. I put them No. 2 because I worry about being hunted, week after week after week. I also think if you look at their schedule, when you’re a heavy favorite it’s hard to stay motivated. They’ve also got some age in a couple of spots. Will DaVante Adams stay healthy? Will Puka Nacua always be available? I love their tight ends, running back, coach and quarterback, but he’s what, 38 years old? I have them at No. 2. 1.Seahawks Cowherd’s thoughts: "What I like about the Seahawks is all their best players are either all going into their athletic prime — Sam Darnold, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Devon Witherspoon — or they’re in their prime. They have no egos. It’s not like the other Seahawks with Pete Carroll, where Marshawn Lynch was a star and Richard Sherman was a star and Russell Wilson was and Pete Carroll was. In his own division, Mike Macdonald is the third-most talked about head coach. Sam Darnold still has that perfect chip on his shoulder. JSN doesn’t get nearly the pub that he should. I think Seattle doesn’t have the brand stars, so they’re still sort of undervalued in the market."

articles.title: The Patriots Are Back: Drake Maye And New England Gets a Chance at Redemption
articles.summary: The wait is finally over, and the New England Patriots are back on the field. The Patriots will open the 2026 NFL season Wednesday night against the Seattle...
articles.body:
The wait is finally over, and the New England Patriots are back on the field.

The Patriots will open the 2026 NFL season Wednesday night against the Seattle Seahawks , but this isn't just another season opener.

It's a rematch of Super Bowl LX , where Seattle defeated New England 29-13 to claim the championship. Now, seven months later, the Patriots get an immediate opportunity to begin their new season against the team that ended their Super Bowl dreams.

For quarterback Drake Maye , this game carries plenty of meaning.

Maye led the Patriots to the Super Bowl last season, but the offense struggled against Seattle's defense when it mattered most. Rather than focusing on revenge, however, Maye and the Patriots have emphasized moving forward and starting the 2026 season on their own terms.

That could be exactly what New England needs.

The Patriots aren't the same team that walked off the field in February.

New England spent the offseason giving Maye more weapons.

The biggest addition was star wide receiver A.J. Brown , who gives Maye another explosive target in the passing game. The Patriots also added wide receiver Romeo Doubs and offensive lineman Alijah Vera-Tucker , while making defensive additions such as safety Kevin Byard and defensive lineman Dre'Mont Jones .

Give Maye everything he needs to take another step forward.

The Patriots' hopes rest heavily on their young quarterback.

Maye enters his third NFL season with significantly more experience and the expectations that come with leading a team that reached the Super Bowl just months ago.

Now, instead of trying to prove New England belongs among the NFL's best, Maye has to prove the Patriots can stay there.

That's a completely different challenge.

The Patriots couldn't have received a more difficult opening assignment.

They have to travel to Seattle and face the defending champions in front of a hostile crowd, less than a year after losing to the Seahawks on the biggest stage.

There are also some immediate injury concerns. Offensive lineman Ben Brown has been ruled out with a knee injury, while running back TreVeyon Henderson remains questionable because of an ankle injury.

Still, the Patriots have a chance to make an early statement.

A win would immediately erase some of the disappointment from Super Bowl LX and announce that New England is ready to make another run.

A loss would raise questions about whether the Patriots can actually take that final step.

The Super Bowl loss is in the past. The roster has changed. Drake Maye has another year of experience.

Now New England gets a chance to start the season exactly where the last one ended — against Seattle.

This time, the Patriots are looking for a different ending.

Head coach Sean McVay told reporters Tuesday the future Hall of Famer will not travel with the team to Australia for Thursday's game against the division-rival San Francisco 49ers.

"The Rams want to give Donald more time to ramp up before making his much-anticipated return after two seasons of retirement," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote.

That Donald needs a bit more time to get ready for game action perhaps shouldn't come as a significant surprise since he last played during the 2023 campaign.

He also has a long-term outlook for the season after coming back to join one of the presumed Super Bowl favorites:

While he won't play in Thursday's game, the defensive tackle is pleased with his progress to this point.

"A couple plays I was a little rusty," Donald said, per ESPN's Sarah Barshop . "It isn't where I want to be, but it's pretty damn good, if you ask me. To not play football in two years, to be moving how I'm moving, like I said, it's really no drop off. It's not where I want to be because I can see it and I know there are things that I want to clean up and I'm going to clean up. The more reps I do, the more I play, it'll get there. But he's still there."

He also said, "I never do anything to be average" and made it clear he still plans on playing at a high level.

And few players in NFL history have reached his level with a resume that includes three Defensive Player of the Year awards, a Super Bowl title, a Defensive Rookie of the Year, eight First-Team All-Pro selections and 10 Pro Bowl nods.

While it may be unrealistic to expect the 35-year-old to still be the best defensive player in the league, the idea of him pairing with Myles Garrett along the defensive line is surely a daunting one for opposing offensive lines.

San Francisco's offensive line can take a deep breath knowing it won't have to deal with him Thursday, although the two teams play again in Week 14.

articles.title: Rams' Aaron Donald won't make game vs. 49ers in Australia after coming out of retirement
articles.summary: Aaron Donald isn't making the trip to Melbourne with the Rams this week after all.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald 's gameday return to the Los Angeles Rams will have to wait.

Donald is not traveling with the Rams to Melbourne this week and will be inactive for L.A.'s season opener against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday (8:35 p.m. ET, Netflix) in Australia, head coach Sean McVay confirmed Tuesday.

It's unclear when Donald will be ready to make his on-field debut with the team this season, though the franchise apparently wanted more time for him to ramp back up after he came out of retirement to rejoin the club in late August.

"I think he'll be ready to go sooner rather than later, but we're making a decision that we think is best for him and for our team," McVay said, via the OC Register's Benjamin Royer . "Being two years off retirement, he's attacked this the right way, but it would have been a really quick turnaround [to play in Australia]."

"I think he'll be ready to go sooner rather than later, but we're making a decision that we think is best for him and for our team," McVay said, via the OC Register's Benjamin Royer .

"Being two years off retirement, he's attacked this the right way, but it would have been a really quick turnaround [to play in Australia]."

Donald and the Rams announced late last month that they had reached a one-year, $20 million deal for him to come out of retirement and play for the team again. Donald missed the past two seasons after he retired in 2024. Donald racked up 111 sacks throughout his career, which is No. 33 on the NFL's all-time list, and he had 53 total tackles during his final season in 2023. He was a huge piece in the Rams' Super Bowl run during the 2021 season, too.

Rumors of Donald's return had been swirling for weeks before he made the decision, especially after the team landed Myles Garrett in a blockbuster trade back in June . Garrett, McVay said on Tuesday, will be ready to play against the 49ers.

Donald, now 35, said when he returned that he had been locked in to his training for the last 13 or 14 weeks, and was testing out his body to make sure he could still physically play professional football. The team has been ramping him up ever since to get him ready for the regular season after he missed nearly all of the preseason. He didn't participate in full 11-on-11 drills until Sunday, too, according to ESPN .

Clearly, Donald and the Rams feel he needs a bit more time to get to where he needs to be to play.

The Rams are flying to Melbourne on Tuesday night, and will land in the country on Thursday morning. They plan to leave shortly after the game on Friday morning local time, too, and will arrive back in Los Angeles less than three days after leaving. While Donald doesn't get to play in the contest, which is the first NFL regular-season game to be held in Australia, he does get to avoid two incredibly long travel days by sitting this one out.

The Rams will host the New York Giants in Week 2 after returning to the United States. That game at SoFi Stadium could be an ideal spot for Donald's debut, especially since the team will play on the road in back-to-back weeks after that.

Regardless, Donald's return will now officially be happening in the United States. When, however, is still unknown.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield reportedly signs 3-year extension with Buccaneers days before season opener
articles.summary: After some training-camp drama, Baker Mayfield has a new deal with the Bucs.
articles.body:
It took a few tense exchanges, but Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally found some common ground. Mayfield reportedly agreed to a three-year extension to remain with the Buccaneers beyond the 2026 season, ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo reported on Tuesday .

Mayfield, 31, is coming off a season in which he threw for 3,693 yards and 26 touchdowns.

The deal comes as Mayfield was set to enter the final year of his contract with the Bucs. But when Mayfield got to training camp, he made it clear he preferred a long-term extension with the team instead of playing on a one-year deal.

The Buccaneers were amenable to the idea, but initially failed to meet Mayfield's needs, causing the quarterback to say the offer was " disappointing " and made him feel "undervalued." In late July, Mayfield said the deadline to negotiate a new deal with the team passed, implying he was no longer open to discussing the issue.

"If you've waited this long to take care of your franchise quarterback," Mayfield said, "that's too bad because it's only going to get worse from here. I am going to have a really good year."

Reports emerged suggesting some members of the front office weren't happy with Mayfield for making those comments. Eventually, general manager Jason Licht said that while the team still preferred to work out a long-term extension with Mayfield, it wasn't opposed to using the franchise tag on Mayfield for the 2027 season.

At that time, Licht also said he understood why Mayfield was upset and frustrated by his previous talks with the team.

Mayfield resurrected his career after signing a one-year, prove-it deal with the Bucs in 2023. Mayfield — a former No. 1 overall pick — was coming off an extremely disjointed 2022, where he started the first five games for the Carolina Panthers before sustaining an injury. By the time Mayfield came back, he was essentially benched. Mayfield asked for his release and was spotted taking reps with the Panthers' scout team in practices .

He was finally granted his release and joined the Los Angeles Rams , who were desperately in need of a starting quarterback after various injuries at the position. Mayfield stepped in and — despite little knowledge of the Rams' offense ahead of time — performed well in the role.

That led to the Buccaneers showing interest in Mayfield the following offseason.

In his first year with the Bucs, Mayfield proved he could still play. He threw for over 4,000 passing yards, adding 28 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. That performance earned him his first-ever Pro Bowl nod. He also led the Bucs to the playoffs, where they won a game before falling in the divisional round.

Mayfield's 2023 comeback earned him a three-year, $100 million extension with the Bucs . He performed even better in 2024, dropping 46 touchdown passes and again making the Pro Bowl. Mayfield saw those numbers decline somewhat in 2025, but was still solid.

All of that led to Mayfield wanting another deal this training camp. And while it briefly looked like both sides were heading for a contentious future divorce, cooler heads prevailed, leading to Mayfield receiving a third contract with Tampa Bay .

articles.title: Baker Mayfield, Bucs Agree to Surprise Contract Extension, Latest Rumors on New Deal
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers reaffirmed their long-term commitment to Baker Mayfield by giving the quarterback a three-year, $165 million contract extension on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers reaffirmed their long-term commitment to Baker Mayfield by giving the quarterback a three-year, $165 million contract extension on Tuesday.

Mayfield signed his last contract in 2024, and its three-year term meant the Bucs would quickly face another decision about prolonging his stay on the Gulf Coast.

General manager Jason Licht told The Athletic's Jeff Howe last July he didn't want the two-time Pro Bowler going anywhere.

"I love Baker. I love everything he's done for us," the GM said. "The goal for us is for Baker to continue to be the player that he is, and at some point, we reach an extension when the time is right and he continues to be our quarterback for a long time. That's the goal."

Days later, Tampa Bay restructured Mayfield's contract, which didn't add any years or new money.

Heading into the 2026 season, the lack of an extension became a more contentious point from the player's perspective.

Mayfield didn't hide his frustration over failing to make a breakthrough before training camp.

"So, disappointing in that regard to not have … to feel disrespected a little bit," he told reporters . "That's really the disappointing part, to feel undervalued after thinking you've earned it. This is not a 'poor me' thing. There's a lot amount of people who have it way worse off. But I can sit here and look at other quarterbacks and peers and evaluate myself based on that and put myself in certain categories that I deserve to be compensated for that."

The 31-year-old far surpassed everyone's expectations in his first season with the team, and he showed in 2024 his renaissance was for real. He threw for 4,500 yards and 41 touchdowns, once again helping the Buccaneers win the NFC South.

The Bucs and Mayfield both went backward in 2025.

The team finished 8-9 and was second in the NFC South, losing the tiebreaker with the Carolina Panthers. Mayfield, meanwhile, had 3,693 passing yards and 26 touchdowns to 11 interceptions. However, he actually finished one spot higher in ESPN's QBR (12th; 61.3) than in 2024.

Mike Evans and Chris Godwin combined to log 17 appearances, which dealt an obvious blow to the passing game.

In general, Mayfield's stock didn't drop to a significant degree. He tied with the Seattle Seahawks' Sam Darnold for 14th in the annual QB tiers from The Athletic's Mike Sando . He was in Tier 2 for the second straight year.

"He probably fluctuates from a 3 to a 2, with some (Tier) 1 games in there," one executive told Sando. "A little bit of a reckless play style, a little smaller guy. You saw some wear and tear catch up to him last season. I lean towards a 3."

Since signing with the Bucs, Mayfield has displayed the self-assurance and creativity in the pocket that made him a college football legend at Oklahoma. Maybe he'll never fully live up to his No. 1 overall pick status, but Tampa Bay has every reason to believe he'll continue being an effective starter.

There's some risk as Mayfield gets older, and he has probably hit his ceiling as a fringe top-10 QB. He's unlikely to take another big leap with his performance.

The dilemma from the Bucs is that they had no guarantees of getting an upgrade in the immediate future. They're playing it safe here and taking the sure thing.

articles.title: Patriots rule RB TreVeyon Henderson out for Wednesday's Super Bowl rematch vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: Henderson has been dealing with an ankle injury throughout the preseason.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots have ruled out running back TreVeyon Henderson for Wednesday night's season opener against the Seattle Seahawks .

Henderson has been dealing with an ankle injury throughout the preseason and has been sidelined from practice for two weeks. The move doesn't come as a complete surprise, but the second-year back did travel with New England for the road game, leaving open the possibility of a last-minute change.

With no Henderson, veteran running back Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to see an increased workload against the Seahawks. Stevenson and Henderson were projected to once again share backfield duties, but now Stevenson will be joined in the backfield by third-string RB Corey Kiner .

This will be the first game that Henderson has missed in his career. Last year as a rookie, he played in all 17 games and finished the year with 911 yards and nine touchdowns on the ground. Henderson added 221 yards and another touchdown on 35 receptions.

Seattle stifled New England's run game in the Super Bowl, as neither Henderson now Stevenson could get much going on the ground.

Henderson had six carries for 19 yards, while Stevenson picked up 23 yards on seven carries.

Stevenson was effective in the passing game. He had 40 yards and a touchdown on five receptions. His touchdown was impressive because quarterback Drake Maye was pressured and looked like he was going to scramble, but he basically pushed the ball toward Stevenson, who made an adjustment back to the ball, caught it, and scored.

Stevenson is heading into his sixth career season, all with the Patriots. Last season, he played in 14 games and finished the year with 603 rushing yards and seven touchdowns.

The veteran back has become infamous for his ball-security issues after fumbling seven times in 2024. Stevenson improved and fumbled just three times last season.

New England will hope for a better result against Seattle than it had in the 29-13 Super Bowl loss, even without Henderson. The bigger concern for the second-year running back will be healing enough that he can return to the practice field, and he will hope to take the field in Week 2 when the Patriots play the Pittsburgh Steelers .

articles.title: Bucs' Updated Salary Cap After Baker Mayfield, Vita Vea Contract Extensions
articles.summary: It has been a busy offseason for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
articles.body:
It has been a busy offseason for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday the NFC South team and quarterback Baker Mayfield agreed to a three-year contract extension that means he will no longer be a free agent after the 2026 campaign.

According to Rapoport , it is a three-year extension worth $165 million overall and $55 million per year.

This comes after Schefter reported last month the Buccaneers agreed to a one-year, $30 million extension with defensive tackle Vita Vea that will keep him with the team for the next two seasons. It also gave him $6 million in new money for the 2026 campaign.

As of Tuesday, Over The Cap lists the Buccaneers with $11.3 million in team cap space.

Keeping Mayfield and Vea for multiple years and getting the deals done before the start of the season is quite a turnaround from what the offseason looked like not long ago in Tampa Bay:

As for Mayfield, NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported "The sides weren't that far apart when talks broke off before training camp and, despite Mayfield's unhappiness with the Buccaneers' offer, he and his camp countered with short-term offers. After a long breath, the sides came back to the table and got a deal done."

In July, the quarterback told reporters he would no longer negotiate his contract until after the 2026 season. He also said he felt "disrespected a little bit" that he was "not presented with an offer that's appealing whatsoever."

He continued and said, "That's really the disappointing part—to feel undervalued after thinking you've earned it."

It turns out, Mayfield did earn a new contract.

In three years with Tampa Bay, the Oklahoma product was named to two Pro Bowls and led the team to back-to-back division titles during the 2023 and 2024 campaigns. He helped keep the team among the league's contenders in the post-Tom Brady era and threw for more than 4,000 yards in each of those division-title seasons.

Mayfield wasn't quite as individually excellent last season but still completed 63.2 percent of his passes for 3,693 yards, 26 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.

With the contract situations out of the way for both Mayfield and one of the defensive leaders in Vea, they and the team can shift their focus toward the season opener.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield reportedly signs 3-year, $165 million extension with Buccaneers days before season opener
articles.summary: After some training-camp drama, Baker Mayfield has a new deal with the Bucs.
articles.body:
It took a few tense exchanges, but Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally found some common ground. Mayfield agreed to a three-year, $165 million extension to remain with the Buccaneers through the 2029 season, according to multiple media reports on Tuesday .

Mayfield, 31, is coming off a season in which he threw for 3,693 yards and 25 touchdowns, rushing for another score.

The deal comes as Mayfield was set to enter the final year of his contract with the Bucs. But when Mayfield got to training camp, he made it clear he preferred a long-term extension with the team instead of playing on a one-year deal.

The Buccaneers were amenable to the idea but initially failed to meet Mayfield's needs, causing the quarterback to say the offer was " disappointing " and made him feel "undervalued." In late July, Mayfield said the deadline to negotiate a new deal with the team passed, implying he was no longer open to discussing the issue.

"If you've waited this long to take care of your franchise quarterback," Mayfield said, "that's too bad because it's only going to get worse from here. I am going to have a really good year."

Reports emerged suggesting some members of the front office weren't happy with Mayfield for making those comments. Eventually, general manager Jason Licht said that while the team still preferred to work out a long-term extension with Mayfield, it wasn't opposed to using the franchise tag on Mayfield for the 2027 season. At that time, Licht also said he understood why Mayfield was upset and frustrated.

Mayfield resurrected his career after signing a one-year, prove-it deal with the Bucs in 2023. Mayfield — a former No. 1 overall draft pick — was coming off an extremely disjointed 2022, when he started the first five games for the Carolina Panthers before sustaining an injury. By the time Mayfield came back, he was essentially benched. Mayfield asked for his release and was spotted taking reps with the Panthers' scout team in practices .

He was finally granted his release and joined the Los Angeles Rams , who were desperately in need of a starting quarterback after various injuries at the position. Mayfield stepped in and — despite little knowledge of the Rams' offense ahead of time — performed well in the role.

That led to the Buccaneers showing interest in Mayfield the following offseason.

In his first year with the Bucs, Mayfield proved he could still play. He threw for more than 4,000 passing yards, adding 28 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. That performance earned him his first Pro Bowl nod. He also led the Bucs to the playoffs, where they won a game before falling in the divisional round.

Mayfield's 2023 comeback earned him a three-year, $100 million extension with the Bucs . He performed even better in 2024, tossing 41 touchdown passes and again making the Pro Bowl. Mayfield saw those numbers decline during an injury-riddled 2025, but he still had Tampa Bay in the mix for another NFC South title.

All of that led to Mayfield wanting another deal this offseason. And while it briefly looked like both sides were heading for a contentious future, cooler heads prevailed, leading to Mayfield receiving a third contract with the Bucs days before their Week 1 road game against the Cincinnati Bengals .

Mayfield will reportedly make $55 million per year on his new deal, the same amount in average annual value that Joe Burrow of the Bengals, Matthew Stafford of the Rams, Jordan Love of the Green Bay Packers , Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars and Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills are earning, per Over the Cap .

articles.title: When Are Top NFL QBs Eligible for Contract Extensions After Baker Mayfield Deal?

articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers signed Baker Mayfield to a three-year, $165 million extension on Tuesday , the largest deal in team history.

It's likely that more quarterback deals are on the horizon, however, as Taylor Bisciotti of NFL Network noted:

Patrick Mahomes once again reset the quarterback market in June when he signed an eight-year restructured deal worth $504.7 million. That deal leads the position in overall value, average annual value ($63 million) and total guaranteed money ($397 million).

Jackson, a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro, is going to expect to be somewhere in that realm. If Williams, Maye and Daniels all have strong seasons, they could be wading in those waters as well. All four signing extensions next offseason could cause the quarterback market to hit astronomical heights.

Stroud is another conversation entirely.

The 24-year-old looked like a future star after his fantastic rookie season in 2023 (4,108 yards, 23 touchdowns, five interceptions). But his passing yards have declined in both seasons since, while he threw for just 39 touchdowns and 20 interceptions between the two campaigns.

Despite that fact, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported last week that the Texans are "prepared to put Stroud in what it feels is a strong place among the 12 quarterbacks in the $50 million club" but he declined. Fowler added that "several people with knowledge of the situation believe Stroud is prepared to play out this season without a new deal, despite Houston making what it considered a competitive offer."

Given Mayfield's recent extension and the possibility of other mega deals next offseason, a rising quarterback market could mean a bigger payday in the future for Stroud. It doesn't come without risk, however, as much will depend on whether Stroud actually has a bounce-back season.

Finally, Nix probably shouldn't be considered in the realm of Williams, Maye and Daniels when it comes to sheer talent or upside, but it's tough to argue with 7,706 yards, 54 touchdowns, 23 interceptions and a 24-10 record through two seasons.

If the Texans were willing to pay Stroud over $50 million a season, it's hard to imagine Nix getting less than $55 million in AAV, which is where players like Josh Allen, Joe Burrow, Matt Stafford and now Mayfield, among others, currently sit. Such is the nature of the quarterback market.

articles.title: Joe Burrow Addresses Bengals Future After Viral 'Now or Never' Comments Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow made it abundantly clear that's he's sticking around for the "long haul" a few weeks after the signal-caller referenced a "now or never" mentality he holds as he hopes to lead his team to a Super Bowl.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow made it abundantly clear that's he's sticking around for the "long haul" a few weeks after the signal-caller referenced a "now or never" mentality he holds as he hopes to lead his team to a Super Bowl.

"I'm efficient with my words, and when I'm efficient with my words, that leaves some room for interpretation," Burrow said in an exclusive interview with Bengals senior writer Geoff Hobson that published Tuesday.

"But I mean what I say. I'm here for the long haul. I'm not going anywhere. I'm just trying to bring a now-or-never mentality to the day-by-day process. If you're not, what are you doing? Attack the day with a championship mindset. The rest will take care of itself."

Last month, Burrow was asked if he was treating the 2026 season as a "now or never" year to win a championship. He responded affirmatively.

"You can keep pushing it down the road or you can talk about it now and say this is the year," Burrow said on Aug. 20, per ESPN's Ben Baby . "You know, I'm tired of saying, 'Next year, next year, next year.' This is it.

"Your life is too short to keep pushing things down the road. I'm trying to instill some urgency and some intensity in everybody to go and be great every day and try to make it happen."

Burrow also added these notes about that sense of urgency, per Baby:

"I'm trying to put it out into the world," Burrow said. "I'm trying to manifest it. I'm trying to show our guys the urgency that I have and that I want us to have as an organization to go and make it happen."

The table is set for the Bengals to rebound after a tough 2025 season, when the team went 6-11, Burrow missed nine games with a Grade 3 turf toe injury, and Cincinnati allowed the third-most points in football (28.9).

Per Sharp Football Analysis , the Bengals have the second-easiest schedule in football this year.

The defense just added a core piece in former New York Giants defensive lineman Dexter Lawrence, a three-time Pro Bowler. Cincinnati also brought in other key defensive pieces, including ex-Seattle Seahawks defensive end Boye Maye and former Minnesota Vikings defensive lineman Jonathan Allen.

The Bengals' offense looks ready to dominate with Burrow back healthy and an elite wide receiver, Ja'Marr Chase, leading the way. Of course, Cincinnati also has a talented running back (Chase Brown) and one of the NFL's best No. 2 wideouts (Tee Higgins) as well.

Burrow clearly has the urgency to win now, and he has every right to feel that way and lead with that optimism.

Cincinnati opens the season on Sunday, 1 p.m. ET at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

articles.body: Gisele Bündchen’s marriage to Tom Brady became one of the most discussed celebrity relationships in sports, especially after Brady reversed his retirement decision in 2022. But while claims about an alleged football-or-family ultimatum spread widely, Bündchen’s own interviews painted a more nuanced picture. Her comments focused on family, presence, personal priorities and the difficult reality of two people growing in different directions.Gisele Bündchen addressed Tom Brady’s NFL returnThe speculation intensified after Brady announced that he would return to the NFL just weeks after initially retiring. Reports at the time suggested the decision created tension at home, with anonymous sources claiming Bündchen wanted Brady to step away from football.One October 2022 report from Us Weekly even quoted an unnamed insider claiming that Bündchen had given Brady an ultimatum. However, that was a source's allegation, not a direct statement from Bündchen.Her own words were considerably more measured.In her September 2022 Elle interview, Bündchen acknowledged that she worried about Brady continuing to play such a demanding sport while raising their children. She said:“Obviously, I have my concerns — this is a very violent sport, and I have my children and I would like him to be more present.”She also made it clear that she understood football was deeply important to Brady. Rather than saying he had to quit, she added:“But ultimately, I feel that everybody has to make a decision that works for [them]. He needs to follow his joy, too.”That distinction matters. Bündchen openly discussed her concerns, but her published comments do not support the dramatic quote circulating online that supposedly describes Brady refusing to choose his family.Gisele Bündchen’s divorce comments tell a deeper storyBündchen also spoke about the years she spent supporting Brady’s career and raising their children. In the same Elle interview, she explained how much of her own life had revolved around creating stability for her family.“I’ve done my part, which is [to] be there for [Tom].”She described moving to Boston and creating a supportive home while Brady pursued football. At the same time, she acknowledged that she had ambitions of her own and wanted to make room for them.Their marriage ultimately ended in October 2022 after 13 years. In her divorce statement, Bündchen said they had “grown apart” and asked for privacy as they moved into separate chapters of their lives.A few months later, Bündchen gave perhaps her clearest explanation in Vanity Fair. Rather than reducing the breakup to one argument about football, she described it as the painful end of a relationship that had changed over time. The interview presented her as someone trying to rebuild her identity while remaining focused on her children.That context is important when evaluating viral posts claiming to reveal what Bündchen supposedly said about Brady. The quotes shown in the screenshot provided earlier do not appear in her verified interviews. articles.body: Reece Weaver’s career has taken a striking turn. After winning fans as a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader on Netflix’s America’s Sweethearts, the 25-year-old is stepping into the very different world of Broadway. Weaver is set to play Roxie Hart in Chicago, trading her cheer uniform for a role built around crime, ambition and scandal, while holding firmly to the values that have shaped her life.Reece Weaver makes a bold Broadway debut as Roxie HartWeaver’s new role pushes her far outside the image viewers know from America’s Sweethearts. Roxie Hart is a seductive character who cheats on her husband and kills her lover, making the part a sharp contrast to Weaver’s cheerful public persona and Christian faith.That difference became clear during rehearsals. Weaver admitted that the production has forced her to use language she rarely used before.“I have never cussed more in my life than these past four weeks,” she said with a giggle.Still, there was one line she refused to cross. Weaver made it clear that she would not use the Lord’s name in vain, even while performing the demanding role.“That’s the one thing I made clear,” Weaver said, sitting outside a coffee shop in Hell’s Kitchen in Manhattan before a rehearsal. “There’s a few times where Roxie said ‘G.D.,’ and I’m like, ‘I can’t say that.’”Her Broadway opportunity arrived at an important moment. Weaver had already decided to leave the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders after Season 3, a decision that surprised many fans. She said an injury featured on the Netflix series was not the reason for her departure.Instead, Weaver wanted to walk away while she still felt grateful for the experience.“I wanted to leave more on a note of gratitude and feeling so full,” she said, “rather than, like, a time of maybe feeling a little burnt out.”That choice also opened another door. Her growing popularity from America’s Sweethearts helped her build an online career, bringing millions of followers and brand opportunities.Reece Weaver and Will Allman navigate life after America’s SweetheartsThe sudden attention has also tested Weaver’s personal life. She and her husband, Will Allman, were still newlyweds when the Netflix series became a hit. Overnight attention brought opinions from strangers, and Weaver said the experience made their relationship feel as though they had to begin again.“I didn’t know how just to navigate my emotions with my reality of trying to be a good wife, trying to be a good teammate, and also people telling me what they think about me on the internet,” Weaver said. “It was just so much.”Therapy helped her manage that pressure, and she said she has stayed away from Reddit for two years.Now, Weaver and Allman are embracing a life that looks nothing like a traditional routine. They moved temporarily to New York with their dog, Ruby, while Weaver prepares for Broadway. Allman has supported her throughout the process, even walking her to and from rehearsals and preparing juices he jokingly calls “Roxtails.”Their unusual lifestyle has also drawn criticism online, particularly after Weaver left the Cowboys Cheerleaders. Allman laughed off the idea that he wanted his wife to stay home.“Nothing in our life is traditional,” he said.For Weaver, Broadway represents another leap into unfamiliar territory. Her dance background gives her confidence, but singing and adapting from a football field to a theater stage have demanded patience. The challenge is new, but so is the opportunity. articles.title: Inspiring story on turning one dream into many: “You need to dream big and understand that you have to work hard” - How Brittany Mahomes keeps reinventing herself
articles.summary: NFL News: For Brittany Mahomes, success has never been about reaching one finish line. Her journey has moved from competitive soccer to fitness, business, women.
articles.body: For Brittany Mahomes, success has never been about reaching one finish line. Her journey has moved from competitive soccer to fitness, business, women’s sports and motherhood, with each chapter opening another door. In a June 2026 interview with Yahoo Entertainment, Mahomes explained the philosophy behind that evolution, offering a message that says as much about the woman she has become as the dreams she still wants to chase.Brittany Mahomes and the lesson behind dreaming bigMahomes delivered her most powerful message while reflecting on how motherhood had changed her outlook. Speaking to Yahoo Entertainment in an interview published June 24, 2026, she explained that becoming a mother had altered the way she viewed her goals, her time and the example she wanted to give her children.“Being a mom changed so many things in my life and changed how I looked at so many things,” she said.That change did not make her ambitions smaller. If anything, it gave them more meaning.She went on to explain that motherhood had made her more intentional and purposeful, while also motivating her to keep moving forward and show her children that limitations do not have to determine their future.Then came the line that captures the heart of her philosophy:“You need to dream big and understand that you have to work hard and do the hard things to do the fun things.”It is a simple message, but there is something revealing about the way Mahomes connects dreaming with work. She does not present ambition as a shortcut to success. For her, the dream is only the beginning.From soccer player to a new kind of sports careerLong before Brittany Mahomes became widely known through the NFL world, soccer was at the center of her life.She played collegiately at the University of Texas at Tyler and later pursued a professional soccer opportunity in Iceland. That chapter did not unfold exactly as she might have imagined when she first stepped onto the field, but it exposed her to something that would become important later: the possibility of building a life around sports without remaining an athlete forever.Her time away from home also helped her discover another interest. During that period, she spent more time working out and creating fitness content, eventually turning that interest into a business direction of its own.That shift is important because it shows what reinvention can actually look like.Sometimes, a dream does not disappear. It changes shape.The soccer player became an entrepreneur. The athlete who once wanted to compete found another way to remain connected to sports. And eventually, that connection brought her into ownership and leadership with the Kansas City Current.Mahomes has described her involvement in women’s sports as something she feels strongly about. “Being able to be involved in the sport, and really help elevate women’s sports, is something that I’m super passionate about,” she said.Her story therefore is not simply about moving from one career to another. It is about carrying lessons from one chapter into the next.How motherhood gave Brittany Mahomes a bigger purposeMotherhood has become the clearest reason behind Mahomes’ desire to keep growing.She and Patrick Mahomes are parents to three children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden. But when Brittany talks about motherhood, she does not only talk about the daily responsibilities of raising a family. She talks about the values she wants her children to witness.That distinction matters.For Mahomes, being a role model does not appear to mean presenting a perfect life. It means allowing her children to see that meaningful goals require patience, effort and courage.She has also acknowledged that motherhood has taught her to become more selective about where she puts her energy.“I think when you become a mom, you learn to say no to things that aren’t as important and focus on what’s best for your life and your family,” she said.That may be one of the most mature parts of her evolution.Reinvention is often described as adding more. In Mahomes’ case, it has also meant learning what to leave out.She does not need every opportunity. She needs the right ones.Her ambitions now sit alongside a family life that has changed her priorities. Rather than viewing those responsibilities as an obstacle to her goals, she appears to see them as part of the reason those goals matter.Brittany Mahomes is building a legacy, not just chasing successThere is another layer to Mahomes’ message about dreaming big.She is no longer chasing dreams simply for herself.The decisions she makes now can become lessons her children carry into their own lives. That gives her ambitions a different kind of weight. A business decision, a role in women’s sports or even the discipline required to keep pursuing a goal can become part of the example she leaves behind.Mahomes has spoken about the importance of having people who believe in her, saying, “Having people around you that believe in you gives you the confidence to continue to dream and dream bigger.”That idea adds another dimension to her journey. Big dreams may begin with individual ambition, but they rarely survive without support.Her story also challenges the idea that reinvention has to happen after failure. Sometimes, reinvention happens because a person succeeds at one thing and realizes there is still more they want to experience.That seems to be the pattern in Mahomes’ life.Soccer opened the first door. Fitness created another. Women’s sports gave her a larger platform. Motherhood gave her a deeper reason to keep going.None of those chapters erased the one before it. They built on it.And perhaps that is why her advice about hard work feels more personal than a generic motivational slogan. Mahomes has lived through the uncomfortable parts of starting again, finding a new direction and figuring out how to balance ambition with responsibility.Her message to her children is ultimately a message about possibility. “You can achieve anything. You can be a part of anything that you want to,” she said.For Brittany Mahomes, dreaming bigger does not mean constantly searching for something better than what she already has. It means refusing to believe that one achievement has to be the final chapter.The dream can change. The role can change. The destination can change. What remains is the willingness to work for it.And that may be the most inspiring part of Brittany Mahomes’ story. She is not trying to fit her life into one definition of success. articles.body: Kylie Kelce has never been shy about discussing the messy, funny and deeply personal parts of motherhood. On her “Not Gonna Lie” podcast, the mother of four recently turned to a subject many new parents may find awkward to discuss openly: intimacy after childbirth. Her comments mixed humor with a blunt reminder that recovery does not end when a baby arrives.Kylie Kelce gets candid about postpartum s*xDuring the March 26, 2026 episode of her podcast, Kylie Kelce spoke about what returning to s*x can feel like after giving birth. Her youngest daughter, Finn, was 11 months old at the time, giving the conversation a personal connection rather than making it a distant discussion about postpartum recovery.Kylie noted that people generally need to wait six to eight weeks before having s*x after childbirth, stressing that healing comes first.“You’re not even allowed to have s*x for six to eight weeks. She’s not ready cause she’s not healed,” Kelce said, while making clear that her comments were based on her experiences with vaginal births.She then delivered the kind of unfiltered observation that has become part of her podcast style.“I’ve had varying experiences, it’s different for every kid. It’s not all fun and games the first couple times, if you catch my drift. We can’t be out here like, ‘Oh that was great,’” she jokingly added. “A human just exited that door.”The joke landed because it captured something often left out of polished conversations about new motherhood. Childbirth can change the body in major ways, and physical recovery does not always follow a neat timetable.Kelce's willingness to say that out loud is part of what makes her discussions resonate. She does not present postpartum life as a smooth transition back to normal. Instead, she talks about the awkwardness, exhaustion and unexpected moments that come with raising children.Her comments also come with an important caveat. Postpartum recovery varies from person to person, and medical guidance should come from a qualified healthcare professional who understands an individual's circumstances.Kylie Kelce jokes about having four childrenThe conversation eventually moved beyond postpartum intimacy and into the bigger question of whether Kylie and Jason Kelce are finished expanding their family.For now, Kylie said that four children feels right. She is raising daughters Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finn with Jason, but she stopped short of making a permanent declaration about having another baby.“I will say Finny is still just cuddly enough that I do not have an urge for a baby right now," Kelce said. “I like to leave it open-ended, because I don’t want the universe to hear me or my uterus.”That playful uncertainty says plenty about her approach to motherhood. She can be content with where her family is while still leaving room for life to surprise her.And then there is Jason.When Kylie explained why people should not wonder too hard about the couple having four children, she turned the spotlight toward her husband’s post-NFL career.“Let me tell you something,” she quipped. “Don’t ever ask yourself why we have four kids. That’s self-explanatory. Turn on ESPN on Monday night.”Jason Kelce, who retired from the NFL and moved into broadcasting, has become a familiar presence on ESPN. Kylie’s joke offered a glimpse into the couple’s playful relationship while also giving listeners another example of the humor that runs through their family life.At its heart, Kylie Kelce’s conversation was not simply about sex after childbirth. It was about honesty. Motherhood can be beautiful and exhausting, intimate and uncomfortable, all at once. By talking about those contradictions without pretending they are glamorous, Kelce continues to make space for conversations that many parents experience but rarely discuss so openly.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Former Washington Football Star Cornerback Turns Heads in Presason
articles.summary: Former Washington CB Tacario Davis is looking to carry momentum into the regular season after an impressive rookie camp.
articles.body:
Over the last decade, Washington has put together an impressive resume of defensive backs who have gone on to have impactful NFL careers. Budda Baker , Trent McDuffie , Kyler Gordon , among others, have helped the Huskies build a reputation for churning out NFL-quality talent in the secondary.

After an impressive rookie training camp with the Cincinnati Bengals , Tacario Davis is in position to add his name to that list. According to the Cincinnati Bengals' depth chart , the lengthy cornerback is currently listed as a backup behind fifth-year veteran Dax Hill. With Hill and fellow starter DJ Turner II entering contract years, the rookie could be in prime position to step into a starting role in the coming years.

According to recent reports, it's highly unlikely Cincinnati will bring back both starters in 2027, giving Davis.

In three preseason games, Davis posted 11 tackles and an interception that came in a strong performance against first-round pick Makai Lemon. After selecting him in the third round of the 2026 NFL draft, Cincinnati is hoping Davis can become a cornerstone piece of its secondary.

When defensive coordinator Al Golden was asked about the UW star, he was quick to praise the 6-foot-4 Arizona transfer.

"He made a really nice interception just before we broke into seven-on-seven. He's another guy with a good football mind, and he's learning quickly," said Golden.

In just a few months in his new home, the young corner has had no issue making his presence felt in the secondary thanks to his ball-hawking ability and intimidating frame. With the Bengals coming off a season where they ranked just 26th in total passing defense, adding a promising young talent could prove to be a difference-maker not just this season, but in the years to follow.

The Bengals kick off their 2026 campaign on Sunday, September 13, at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
