articles.title: Buccaneers news: Why Baker Mayfield's $165 million extension is a great move
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers did not make a reckless bet by giving Baker Mayfield a three-year, $165 million contract extension. They made the investment to keep...
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers did not make a reckless bet by giving Baker Mayfield a three-year, $165 million contract extension. They made the investment to keep their franchise quarterback during a period of transition.

Mayfield's extension keeps him under contract through 2029, with the three added seasons averaging $55 million annually. It is the largest contract in Buccaneers franchise history. Those numbers create immediate sticker shock, especially after the team finished 8-9 and missed the playoffs last season.

However, quarterback contracts cannot be evaluated without considering production and replacement cost. The Buccaneers have undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels behind Mayfield. Allowing their established starter to leave would have sent them searching for an answer at the sport's most important position without a clear successor already on the roster.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Mayfield deserves more credit than one disappointing season suggests. Across his first three years with the Buccaneers, he threw for 12,237 yards and 95 touchdowns. These totals rank third and second, respectively, across the NFL over that span. He also led Tampa Bay to two NFC South championships and two playoff appearances.

His 2024 performance showed the level he can reach when healthy. Mayfield completed 71.4 percent of his passes for 4,500 yards and 41 touchdowns, establishing career highs in all three categories. Quarterbacks capable of producing at that level rarely become available, and they cost more when they do.

The 2025 regression still matters. Tampa Bay started 6-2 before collapsing to 8-9, while Mayfield's production declined as he played through knee, biceps, and shoulder injuries. His supporting cast was depleted, too. That context does not excuse every poor decision or late-season mistake. It does make dismissing his previous two seasons an overreaction.

Tampa Bay avoided the risk of Mayfield rebuilding his value during 2026 and entering free agency with greater leverage. A rebound season could have forced the Buccaneers into a bidding war, an expensive franchise tag, or another uncertain quarterback search. Securing him now provides cost certainty before the market climbs again.

The commitment is not excessively long, either. Mayfield is 31, and the extension carries him only through his age-34 season. Tampa Bay is paying for his prime rather than guaranteeing money deep into his late thirties.

That stability becomes even more valuable as the offense adjusts to its fifth coordinator in five seasons and moves forward without longtime receiver Mike Evans beside him. Mayfield has produced through repeated offensive changes, earned the locker room's trust, and embraced being the face of the franchise. The price is substantial because competent quarterback play is expensive. For the Buccaneers, the greater risk would have been letting the right quarterback leave without a credible plan to replace him.

articles.title: Charlotte Wilder, Mina Kimes discuss how Dianna Russini scandal opened door for ‘people looking for an excuse’ to target women
articles.summary: The legacy of the Dianna Russini scandal is still taking shape, as we near the first NFL kickoff since her alleged affair with New England Patriots head coac...
articles.body:
The legacy of the Dianna Russini scandal is still taking shape, as we near the first NFL kickoff since her alleged affair with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel was revealed and await Russini's personal account.

But one immediate ramification of Russini's lapse in judgment seems to be a chilling effect among some women NFL reporters, who ESPN reported this week have felt hesitant to take public meetings with coaches for fear of how they will be viewed.

The conversation began as a hypothetical way back in April, shortly after Page Six published photos showing Russini and Vrabel together at a resort in Arizona. At the time, USA Today's Nancy Armour suggested in a column that Russini had jeopardized the credibility of all women in sports media with her actions. Dozens of women in the industry disagreed with Armour , calling it unfair that Russini's mistake would undermine anyone else based solely on gender .

This week on The Sports Gossip Show , host Charlotte Wilder and ESPN's Mina Kimes shared their perspective on ESPN's update indicating that women who cover teams are navigating their jobs differently as a result of the scandal.

"I think it reflects sort of a broader thing that happens in any industry, which is when someone who's not in the majority makes any sort of error, it becomes a referendum for their entire class. And I think that's just kind of what's happening here," Kimes said.

"Giving license to male sports fans generally to speak about them a certain way, or to honestly talk about this story in a way that they don't with other stories involving lapses in journalism. It's been interesting to watch on the Russini side of it, this massive conversation on the internet about, 'This is a crime against journalism, and no one's talking about it' … it's kind of hard to take those critiques in good faith when they're clearly not coming from a place of, these aren't people who actually care about journalism.

"They're not applying those standards to things that other insiders do, perhaps."

While Kimes did not name specific other insiders or their breaches, many others around sports media have noted this hypocrisy throughout the Russini scandal. It has been difficult for some to see past the allegations of infidelity and the salacious images published by tabloids to address the underlying questions around insiders and what they do to gain access.

And indeed, far more voices have weighed in on this particular tabloid story and the questions it has raised about journalistic integrity than usual. Wilder argued the scandal has revealed a double standard among insiders .

"It seems to me that to blame one woman for making a mistake and saying that she has screwed it up for everybody else, nobody does that for men," Wilder said. "I understand that it is different; she was in a very high-profile position, but it doesn't sit right, I don't think."

The scandal has also, Wilder added, given bad actors an opening to bash a prominent woman in the industry.

"It gives license to people, perhaps, who are looking for an excuse to not treat women the same way, and then run with it," she said. "And then the women are the ones who bear the brunt of it. So yes, there is a ripple effect. I just wish the correct people were blamed, as well, for it."

Both Wilder and Kimes reported on the NFL earlier in their careers before transitioning into on-air roles.

This is a useful conversation to have about insiders, women who cover sports, and even accountability in the pressure cooker of professional athletics. Hopefully, as the allegations facing Vrabel and Russini fade into memory, we can have that conversation rather than the juicier, more unserious one that has taken up more attention this summer.

articles.title: NFL legend Edgerrin James seeks support for son Jizzle amid unspecified substance abuse battle
articles.summary: Edgerrin James urged fans not to give his son Jizzle James money or valuables, saying the college basketball transfer is battling a substance abuse issue.
articles.body: This story may contain details that are disturbing.If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988. Pro Football Hall of Famer Edgerrin James turned to social media in a public plea for his son, former Charlotte basketball player Jizzle James. The former Indianapolis Colts standout running back said his son is facing a substance abuse issue. James did not share further details about the issue. He did, however, ask anyone who sees his 21-year-old son to offer him a hug while urging them not to give him anything of value. "Jizzle is dealing with substance abuse and is NOT in the right state of mind right now," James wrote Tuesday in an Instagram Story post. James emphasized that his son’s needs are being met and urged those around him to offer encouragement and love. "You’re not helping him by feeding the problem. He wants/needs for NOTHING. Give him a hug. Give him encouragement. Give him love. THAT’S IT. Be patient with him. We’re fighting for him, not against him." James’ stint as a college basketball player at Charlotte was brief. After spending three seasons with Cincinnati, he transferred to the 49ers earlier this offseason to follow Wes Miller, who left the Bearcats to become Charlotte’s head coach. According to Charlotte’s sports information department, James is no longer with the program. A spokesperson cited personal issues. James’ exit from Charlotte followed a turbulent final season with Cincinnati. The Bearcats dismissed him from the program last summer but reinstated him midway through the season. He appeared in 23 games, averaging 10.9 points and 2.1 assists per game. James averaged 10.8 points per game during his Cincinnati career. articles.title: Oregon football news: How Dante Moore can stand out in loaded 2027 NFL Draft class
articles.summary: The No. 6 Oregon Ducks escaped Week 1 with a close-call 34-27 win over the Boise State Broncos. While it was a closer contest than the Ducks probably would h...
articles.body:
The No. 6 Oregon Ducks escaped Week 1 with a close-call 34-27 win over the Boise State Broncos. While it was a closer contest than the Ducks probably would have liked, it was still a strong showing from Dante Moore . His spectacular performance was another example why he should be one of the top quarterbacks taken in the 2027 NFL Draft class, but what can he do to stand out amongst the crowd?

During a guest appearance on "Football 301," NFL Draft analyst Dane Brugler of The Athletic and Nate Trice of Yahoo! Sports, agree that continuing to add weight would be largely beneficial for the Ducks' redshirt senior. They both would like to see Moore clean up his work from the pocket, but overall, getting bigger should help the Oregon star rise up draft boards.

"The thing that helped me from like, really just going, 'Okay, this guy can ascend,' one, he already gained weight, which is good" Trice said. "That was one thing I wanted to see. Was [Moore] gain weight and strength, because I thought in the pocket he can get a little scrunched up as it kinda got mucky on him…

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I'm glad you mentioned the size," Brugler responded. "That's something that worried me last [year]. He looked like he was what? 205 [lbs] last year? He just looked small in the pocket. This year, I was talking to a scout a few weeks ago, he said [Moore is] up to 215 and he wants to be around 218 as his normal playing weight, and that's a big difference."

Dante Moore finished Week 1 with 378 passing yards and three touchdowns while completing 28 of his 37 attempts, giving him a 75.6% completion percentage. That's the type of outing that will catch the attention of NFL scouts, especially if he can maintain that level of play throughout this season.

Oregon's star quarterback will have another opportunity to rise NFL Draft boards in Week 2. The Ducks are scheduled to face off against the Oklahoma State Cowboys for the first road game of the campaign.

articles.title: Cody Ford, ex-Bengals swing tackle, gets Bills' tryout
articles.summary: Former Cincinnati Bengals offensive lineman Cody Ford worked out Sept. 8 for the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Former Cincinnati Bengals offensive lineman Cody Ford worked out Sept. 8 for the Buffalo Bills .

Ford, a swing tackle for the Bengals, was cut by Cincinnati in August.

Ford played his first three NFL seasons for the Bills, and was a second-round pick of Buffalo in the 2019 NFL Draft.

Photos: Bengals practice ahead of season opener against Tampa Bay

He played in 50 games over the past three seasons for the Bengals.

In 2025, Ford had a 21-yard reception on his 29th birthday during the third quarter of the team's NFL Week 17 win against Arizona at Cincinnati's Paycor Stadium.

Earlier in the game, Ford replaced an injured Amarius Mims at offensive tackle.

In August 2025, Ford was injured during training camp.

In August, the Bills released former Bengals safety Geno Stone .
